common_name: Coronation Gold Yarrow (Classic Golden Cut-Flower Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in very well-drained, lean, dry to moderately moist soil in full sun; Coronation Gold requires excellent drainage and will not tolerate heavy clay or wet soil, particularly during humid Gulf South summers.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, dry to moderately moist soil in full sun; Coronation Gold is one of the classic, longest-cultivated hybrid yarrow cultivars, a cross involving Achillea filipendulina prized for its dense, perfectly flat-topped heads of rich mustard-gold flowers held on sturdy, upright stems above finely cut, silvery-gray, aromatic foliage. It blooms over a long season from early to midsummer and is a superb cut and dried flower — the sturdy stems and long-lasting color make it one of the most reliable yarrows for fresh arrangements and for hanging to dry, retaining good color for months. Award of Garden Merit-winning and long a garden standard, it is extremely drought- and heat-tolerant, thriving in lean, poor soils where richer perennials struggle, though good drainage is essential — soggy soil, not heat, is what causes trouble in humid Southern summers. Deadhead spent flower heads to encourage additional bloom, and divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor and good flower production.
